test_title: PYST 32: SSC CGL 2025 - General Knowledge (Held On: 22th_September_2025_Shift_2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following temple architectural features is characteristic of the Nagara style, especially found in central and northern India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Shikhara**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• The **Nagara style of temple architecture**, prominent in northern and central India, is distinguished by its **Shikhara**, which is a towering, curvilinear superstructure constructed above the sanctum sanctorum (garbhagriha). 
• The **Shikhara** is a defining feature of Nagara temples, characterized by its **vertical emphasis and intricate carvings**. It often has multiple tiers or storeys, enhancing its majestic appearance. 
• **Shikhara** typically culminates in a decorative element known as the **amalaka**, a circular or disc-like structure symbolizing the link between the earthly and celestial realms. 
• The Nagara style lacks the elaborate gateways (**Gopuram**) found in the Dravidian style of southern India, making the **Shikhara** its most prominent architectural component. 
• The temples in **Khajuraho**, **Konark**, and **Rajarani Temple** in Odisha are exemplary representations of the Nagara style, with their intricate **Shikhara** structures. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Vimana:** 
• It is a feature of **Dravidian temple architecture**, primarily found in southern India. 
• Unlike the curvilinear **Shikhara**, the **Vimana** is pyramidal and consists of progressively smaller storeys. 
• The temples in Tamil Nadu, such as the **Brihadeeswarar Temple**, showcase the **Vimana**. 
• **Mandapa with Barrel Vaults:** 
• Mandapas are pillared halls in Indian temple architecture, serving as a space for congregational activities. 
• The barrel vault feature is more common in Buddhist and Jain architectural styles rather than the Nagara style. 
• **Gopuram:** 
• Gopuram is a towering gateway primarily associated with **Dravidian temples**, such as those in Tamil Nadu. 
• These gateways are adorned with intricate sculptures and serve as entrances to temple complexes. 
• Examples include the **Meenakshi Temple** and **Sri Ranganathaswamy Temple**. 
• **Nagara Style Characteristics:** 
• The Nagara style of architecture flourished between the **6th and 13th centuries**. 
• It is primarily found in regions such as **Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Odisha, and Uttar Pradesh**. 
• The temples often have multiple **Shikharas**, intricate carvings, and lack boundary walls. 
• Prominent examples include the **Sun Temple** in Konark and the **Kandariya Mahadeva Temple** in Khajuraho. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Shikhara Variants:** 
• In the Nagara style, there are three main types of **Shikharas**: **Rekha-Prasad** (curvilinear), **Phamsana** (rectangular), and **Valabhi** (barrel-shaped). 
• The **Rekha-Prasad** is the most prominent and recognizable form of **Shikhara**. 
• **Symbolism:** 
• The **Shikhara** symbolizes Mount Meru, believed to be the axis of the universe in Hindu cosmology. 
• The decorative **amalaka** on top further represents cosmic harmony and spiritual transcendence. 
• **Historical Development:** 
• The Nagara style evolved during the Gupta period and reached its zenith during the **Chandela dynasty** in the 10th-11th centuries. 
• Its architectural innovations influenced subsequent styles across northern and central India. 
• **Regional Variations:** 
• While the Nagara style is unified by the **Shikhara**, regional variations include distinct ornamentation and structural designs. 
• For instance, Odisha temples often have intricately carved exteriors, while Rajasthan temples showcase bold and dynamic forms. </ul
